summary: A reminder from BBN about scheduled IMP software releases. IMPs can be reloaded between 7 and 8 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday, in addition to hardware maintenance. An IMP going down message is sent to all hosts at the site about an hour before.

eli5.summary: A reminder that the network machines may restart early on Tuesday mornings, and that they will warn you first.

questions: when were imps reloaded in the arpanet
what is the imp going down message
subtitle: BBN's reminder that IMPs may be reloaded on Tuesday mornings, and how hosts get warned.

tldr.problem: Sites needed to know when IMP software could be reloaded and how they would be warned.
tldr.mechanism: BBN reserves 7 to 8 a.m. eastern time every Tuesday for reloads and sends an IMP-Going-Down message to hosts with the reason, timing and duration.
tldr.outcome: The note updates RFC 381 and re-emphasizes two points of its scheduling procedures.

today: RFC 406 updates RFC 381 and has no recorded replacement. It describes an early ARPANET maintenance practice.

sections.title: Scheduling Reminder
sections.content: The note reminds readers that the procedures suggested in RFC 381 for scheduling IMP software maintenance had been in effect for about two months. Two points needed re-emphasis.
sections.eli5: A friendly reminder of the rules that were set up two months earlier.

sections.title: The Tuesday Window and Warnings
sections.content:
First, BBN reserves the hour from 7 to 8 a.m. eastern time every Tuesday for reloading IMPs. It will probably not use the period every Tuesday, but it reserves it every Tuesday. This is in addition to the hardware preventive maintenance scheduled at each site.

Second, an IMP-Going-Down message is sent to all hosts at the site, giving the time, expected duration and reason. BBN tries to send it an hour before software releases and five to ten minutes before scheduled preventive maintenance, and notifies hosts when possible before unscheduled stops. Thirty seconds before the IMP goes down, a second message says it is going down immediately.
sections.eli5: Tuesday early morning is set aside for restarts. You get a warning an hour before, and another just before the switch-off.

sections.title: The IMP-Going-Down Message
sections.content:
The message is 32 bits. Bits 1 to 4 are all zero, bits 5 to 8 are 0010 and bits 9 to 16 are all zero. Bits 17 to 32 carry the details.

  • All bits zero: going down in 30 seconds.
  • Bits 17, 18 = 01: scheduled hardware PM.
  • Bits 17, 18 = 10: scheduled software reload.
  • Bits 17, 18 = 11: emergency reload on restart.
  • Bits 19 to 22: how soon the IMP is going down, in 5 minute units.
  • Bits 23 to 32: how long it will be down, in 5 minute units.
sections.eli5: The warning is a tiny coded note. Part of it says why, part says how soon, and part says how long.

fields.name: Reason
fields.desc: Bits 17, 18: 01 hardware PM, 10 software reload, 11 emergency reload.

references.text: RFC 381, procedures for scheduling IMP software maintenance.
